newsitem.title: LIECHTENSTEIN: Russia condemns new U.S. strikes on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Russia condemns new U.S. strikes on Iraq.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov hit out at the United States over its continuing missile strikes against Iraq, saying the action could bring "catastrophic consequences" on the world scene.

Use of force by one country without the approval of the United Nations Security Council "could lead to anarchy in international relations," he told reporters in the Liechtenstein capital, where he came to sign a cultural agreement.
Primakov, speaking after talks with the Alpine principality's foreign minister Andrea Willi, said Russia saw the second round of U.S. attacks on military targets in Iraq "very negatively."
"Such a system could lead to catastrophic consequences," he declared. "I am speaking not only about regional affairs, but about the world order.

"No single country can take action that could disrupt the world order. There is the U.N. Security Council, and only this can decide on using force....No-one can disrupt this world order or it could lead to anarchy in international relations."

It was the second condemnation of the U.S. attacks from Primakov, who for years under the old Soviet Union was an academic specialist on the Middle East who frequently met Iraq's President Saddam Hussein.

Commenting in the Swiss capital Berne on the first wave of strikes, he told a news conference on Tuesday that the assault could heighten tension across the Middle East and called for them to be stopped immediately.
"I hope this action will not be repeated and that good sense will prevail," he said after talks with Switzerland's Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti.
In those remarks, Primakov also suggested the raids were launched as much to boost President Bill Clinton's chances in the November U.S. presidential elections.
The attacks, he said in Berne, "cannot be supported by anyone at all, except those who put domestic politics, including pre-electoral questions, above all else."
After those comments, the Russian government in Moscow also condemned the strikes, saying they were unacceptable and calling for an end to "all military actions in Iraq threatening its sovereignty."
